traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 109 Cucurbitaceae: herbs, rarely undershrubs, with watery sap, often rough; stems climbing or trailing, mostly with coiled tendrils; flowers of one sex, on one plant or on two; stamens mostly 3, rarely 1 to 5; ovary inferior, very rarely free, its placentas often 3; ovules numerous. Alternate leaves, 5-merous regular flowers and the berry (the pepo of melons and gourds) are from common knowledge, inferred, not traced; the copy read garbles the sentence on the flowers' symmetry.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 335, 336, family Cucurbitaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral; read as "spiral".

traits.leaf_division.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 335, 336, family Cucurbitaceae: leaf division simple; read as "simple".

traits.leaf_venation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 335, 336, family Cucurbitaceae: leaf venation palmate; read as "palmate".

traits.leaf_incision.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 335, 336, family Cucurbitaceae: leaf incision lobed, palmately, often; read as {"lobed": "often"}.

traits.stipules.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 335, 336, family Cucurbitaceae: stipules false; read as false.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Cucurbitaceae: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded usually tubers. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.
